summary: Picking Lower third now moves the captions low on the left, with the plate on the title-safe guide, bold white on the mock's violet plate. Picking another style puts them back where they were. A film written out draws them in the same place.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next, no switch changed from its default. Any recording with speech, captions written (timeline + menu, Captions).

try.do: Open a recording with speech and write its captions. They sit centred on a dark plate.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: In the Captions section, click the Lower third tile.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Compare with the mock's Lower third (video-captions.html, canvas preview with Lower third picked).
Change the caption font or size, then pick Lower third again: your font and size stay.
Export the video with captions Burned in and look at any frame.
Click the Caption tile: the captions go back to where they were, centred.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

evaluate: Does Lower third now read as a different style from Caption at a glance?
Is the violet plate close enough to the mock's, or should it follow the accent colour instead?
If you moved the lower third yourself and then pick Caption, is going back to where the captions were before the right answer?
Is the soft drop under the plate the right weight over a busy recording?
rough: Plate colour matches the mock: violet #9A5CFF to lilac #C56CFF at 120 degrees, chosen over the design system's accent.
The mock's small Lower-third tag on the plate's top edge is not drawn yet: a-lower-third-wears-the-mock-s-lower-third-badge.
The mock sets the lower third in New York serif; the app keeps the font you chose, as every style does since captions-are-one-layer-positioned-and-styled-lik.

The plate sits on the same floor every caption sits on, a little above the drawn title-safe line, where the mock has it on that line; that floor is shared with every style since captions-are-one-layer-positioned-and-styled-lik.
The Background colour well shows only the plate's first colour; picking a colour makes the plate one flat colour.
